author: blu
body: The default FileSystem handler stubs. Emitted only when the program cites FileSystem -- read-text always appears in that effect's definition, so its handler slot existing is exactly the signal that the servicer workers (fat16-servicer-read / -write, in FileSystem.codex, which cites Fat16) are present to be called. A program that never names the effect emits neither stub, so its finalize carries no unresolved reference to a worker it does not have.

author: blu
body: Each stub is the compiler's default discharge for one FileSystem op. It checks the running process's direction bit (cap-filesystem-read for a read, -write for a write) against its own capability word -- so a program GRANTED FileSystem.Read that performs write-file is refused here, which is the runtime half of the grant that nothing enforced before. On a pass it raises the kernel fs-elevated cell, which the block syscalls honour in place of cap-block-device (emit-block-elev-gate), calls the fat16 worker, and lowers the cell again. The elevation is inline and has no callable name of its own on purpose: a bare elevate primitive would let any program raise the cell and then drive block-write-sector directly, which is the exact bypass this design exists to close. The stub is safe to name because it gates itself before it elevates. Path scope is not re-checked here; fat16 already enforces it (fat16-scope-admits).

author: blu
body: The dump is frame-free and prints only through the data-channel serial primitives the exception dump uses. Its original form printed the header through the control channel (which nothing services in a standalone run, so the ready-spin hung forever) and inlined emit-print-text, whose alloc-local frame slots stomp the caller's frame inside a frameless helper. Counts and samples print as hex qwords: PROF:<count> then one PROF:<rip> line per sample. Returns the sample count.

author: blu
body: The 32-bit MMIO pair reaches memory the same way poke-32 does, so it carries the same window guard. Without it, Device.Mmio would be a way around Gpu.Memory: a chapter that declared the board row could write the rasterizer's command buffer through read-mmio-32 and poke-mmio-32 and never earn bit 18. These are driver-rate, not memo-rate, so the guard costs them nothing worth counting.
